misconceptions.description: Presenting a studio package that skips a link in the finding-to-principle-to-decision-to-evidence-to-revision chain
misconceptions.trigger: learner jumps from a research finding straight to a finished prototype with no design decision or evidence connecting them
misconceptions.feedback: Make every link visible: finding, principle, design decision, evidence, disclosed revision. A skipped link breaks the translation argument.

misconceptions.description: Citing research that never changes any design decision, treating the citation itself as research translation
misconceptions.trigger: package names a principle but the design contradicts or ignores it
misconceptions.feedback: Show where the cited research changed the design. A citation that leaves the design unchanged is decoration.

misconceptions.description: Offering a reasonable path from finding to design as if it were proof that the design decision worked
misconceptions.trigger: package has finding and decision and polish but no evidence that the decision produced the intended effect
misconceptions.feedback: Add the evidence link. A plausible translation still needs a tested result, not just a well-argued intent.
